traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA Phyllanthaceae (read 2026-10-17): plants hermaphrodite, monoecious or dioecious, flowers mostly unisexual; no ranking given. Our genus weighting (approximate sizes, not read this session): Phyllanthus s.l. incl. Glochidion and Breynia (~1,200, chiefly monoecious) plus Cleistanthus and Bridelia exceed the dioecious Antidesma, Baccaurea, Aporosa, Uapaca, Flueggea and Margaritaria (~400).

traits.leaf_incision.note: Wikipedia Phyllanthaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves simple (compound only in Bischofia) with entire margins; no lobing mentioned. DELTA has no separate Phyllanthaceae page.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia Phyllanthaceae (read 2026-10-17): margin almost always entire, only rarely toothed. Phyllanthus holds over half the family's species.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Phyllanthaceae (read 2026-10-16): spiral or distichous. 'distichous usually' is my weighting: Phyllanthus (~1,200 spp.) bears two-ranked leaves on flattened leafy branchlets.

traits.perianth.note: DELTA Phyllanthaceae (read 2026-10-17; ~2,050 spp, 56 genera, a preliminary draft): perianth either calyx plus corolla or calyx only, petals often lacking. Weighted by genus size (approximate, not read this session): apetalous Phyllanthus s.l. with Glochidion and Breynia (~1,200), Antidesma, Baccaurea, Aporosa and Uapaca (~350 together) far outweigh the petalled Cleistanthus, Bridelia, Andrachne and Amanoa (~250). A calyx-only flower maps to tepals. Re-ranks the earlier value, from floral-diagrams, whose top states were tied.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 261: perianth mostly 5-merous, sometimes 3- to 9-merous.

traits.stamens.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 260: Ronse De Craene general formula: stamens 2 to 35, one whorl usually alternating with the petals.

traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 260, 261: carpels 3 or 2, always 3 in 5-merous flowers; general formula 1 to 15.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 133 Euphorbiaceae, which holds what APG sets apart as Phyllanthaceae (Phyllanthus, Bridelia, Antidesma, Aporosa, Baccaurea, Hymenocardia, the genera with paired ovules): leaves alternate, simple, mostly with stipules; flowers unisexual, the sexes on one plant or on two; petals mostly absent; ovary superior, of three cells; fruit a capsule or a drupe (Baccaurea's a berry). Library 1.0's family is 82% trees and shrubs. The ovary's place and the berry are inferred, not traced.
